_note: These need a machine with nix, KVM and systemd-run --user, and network access. Eval 2 needs a human for the emailed code; run it attended.

evals.prompt: Use our browser to open https://example.com, follow its one link, and tell me the title of the page you land on. Send me a screenshot too.
evals.expected_output: Checks the VM is up (starts it if not), opens the page in a tab, finds and clicks the link, reports the landing page's URL and title, and saves a screenshot it then views.
expectations: scripts/browser-vm is used (status or up, then tab commands) rather than a browser on the host
The page is read (text or elements) before the click
The reported title and URL come from the tab after the click
A screenshot file is saved and opened with the Read tool
The tab opened for the task is closed at the end

evals.prompt: log into the demo account at https://the-internet.herokuapp.com/login with our browser. the credentials are in the password manager under 'herokuapp demo'
evals.expected_output: Looks the item up in the password manager, fills the username, pipes the password over stdin, submits, confirms the secure-area page, and never prints the password.
expectations: The password manager is searched for the item before the user is asked for credentials
The password reaches the page through --stdin, not as a command argument
The password is never echoed, printed or written to a file
Success is confirmed from the page after submitting (text or wait), not assumed
If the password manager is locked or the item is missing, the user is asked rather than a guess being typed

evals.prompt: is the browser vm actually isolated from this machine? and can it get through the recaptcha on https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api2/demo
evals.expected_output: Runs isolation-check and quotes it, states the in-guest-firewall limit, then opens the demo, waits for the extension to solve the challenge, and reports whether a response token appeared and how long it took.
expectations: isolation-check is run and its output is quoted, not paraphrased from the skill text
The answer states that the egress block is a firewall inside the guest, and names what the check does not test
The challenge is left to the extension: nothing is clicked inside the CAPTCHA frame
The result is taken from the response token's length, with a wait of up to two minutes
If no NopeCHA key is imported, the reply says so and asks for one instead of reporting a generic failure
